Interviewer: Some people tell us that they've reached a crossroads at some points in their life where multiple paths were available, and their choice then made a significant difference in defining who they are. What about you? Was there a moment like that for you, and if so, could you tell me the whole story about that from start to finish?

Agent: A significant crossroads in my life occurred during my sophomore year of college when I had to choose between pursing a more traditional career in business or follow my passion for environmental conservation. I remember spending a lot of time in nature, reflecting on what truly made me happy. In the end, I chose to switch my major to environmental science, and that decision has shaped my career and personal convictions ever since.

Interviewer: Some people tell us that they've reached a crossroads at some points in their life where multiple paths were available, and their choice then made a significant difference in defining who they are. What about you? Was there a moment like that for you, and if so, could you tell me the whole story about that from start to finish?

Agent: Yes, I faced a crossroads when I graduated from university. I had two job offers: one in my hometown and another in a bustling city on the East Coast. It was a tough decision because staying near my family was tempting, but I was excited about the opportunities and lifestyle the city job promised. I ultimately chose to move to the city, which launched my career in a new direction and enriched my life with diverse experiences.

Interviewer: Do you think another person or an organization could have lent a helping hand during moments like these?

Agent: I believe that organizations like career counseling services could have been more proactive in helping students explore different fields and interests earlier in their academic life. Personal mentors from related fields would have also been beneficial during that decision-making process.

Interviewer: Are there anyone else in your immediate family whom you have not mentioned? Who are they, and what is your relationship with them like?

Agent: Besides my partner and daughter, my immediate family includes my parents and two younger sisters. We are very close, even though they still live back in Colorado. We keep in touch regularly and visit each other during holidays and special occasions.

Interviewer: Are there anyone else in your immediate family whom you have not mentioned? Who are they, and what is your relationship with them like?

Agent: Aside from my parents who still live in my hometown, I have a few cousins I'm close to, even though we don’t see each other often. We maintain a strong connection through regular phone calls and social media.

Interviewer: Now let's talk about your current neighborhood. Tell me all about the neighborhood and area in which you are living now.

Agent: I currently live in a vibrant neighborhood in Portland, Oregon. It is a diverse and welcoming community with an eclectic mix of people. Our area has plenty of green spaces, local markets, and cozy cafes. People here are friendly and there's a strong sense of community.

Interviewer: Tell me about the people who live with you right now, even people who are staying here temporarily.

Agent: I live with my roommate, Alex, who is a permanent member of the household.

Interviewer: Is anyone in your household a temporary member, or is everyone a permanent member of the household?

Agent: Everyone in my household is a permanent member.

Interviewer: Tell me about anyone else who stays here from time to time, if there is anyone like that

Agent: Occasionally, my cousin stays over when they visit the city for work, but it's not very frequent.

Interviewer: Tell me about anyone else who stays here from time to time, if there is anyone like that

Agent: Occasionally, my parents visit and stay with us for a few days.

Interviewer: Is there anyone who usually lives here but is away - traveling, at school, or in a hospital?

Agent: No, there is no one who usually lives here but is currently away.

Interviewer: Right now, across a typical week, how do your days vary?

Agent: My weekdays are fairly structured with work from 9 to 5, but weekends are more flexible and family-focused.

Interviewer: If you have children, tell me about a typical weekday during the school year for your children. What is their daily routine? And what are after school activities your children participate in?

Agent: I don't have children, so there isn't a school-related routine in my household.

Interviewer: If you have children, tell me about a typical weekday during the school year for your children. What is their daily routine? And what are after school activities your children participate in?

Agent: During the school year, the kids wake up at 7 AM and leave for school by 8 AM. After school, they have soccer practice three times a week and piano lessons on Thursdays.

Interviewer: Some people we've talked to tell us about experiences with law enforcement. How about for you?

Agent: I haven't had any direct experiences with law enforcement, fortunately.

Interviewer: Some people we've talked to tell us about experiences with law enforcement. How about for you?

Agent: I haven't had any significant experiences with law enforcement, just routine things like traffic stops.

Interviewer: What other experiences with law enforcement stand out in your mind?

Agent: I remember being pulled over for a minor traffic violation, and the officer was quite respectful and courteous. It stood out because I've heard mixed stories, but my personal experience was positive.

Interviewer: Some people tell us about experiences of arrest - of loved ones, family members, friends, or themselves. How about for you?

Agent: I haven't had experiences of arrest personally or with any close family members, though I've had friends who have been arrested for minor infractions.

Interviewer: How would you describe your political views?

Agent: I would describe my political views as moderate, leaning slightly liberal on social issues.

Interviewer: Tell me about any recent changes in your political views.

Agent: Recently, I've become more concerned about environmental issues and have shifted to supporting more green initiatives.

Interviewer: One topic a lot of people have been talking about recently is race and/or racism and policing. Some tell us issues raised by the Black Lives Matter movement have affected them a lot, some say they've affected them somewhat, others say they haven't affected them at all. How about for you?

Agent: The issues raised by the Black Lives Matter movement have affected me somewhat, as they have made me more aware of systemic inequalities.

Interviewer: How have you been thinking about the issues Black Lives Matter raises?

Agent: I've been thinking about the issues Black Lives Matter raises in terms of how we can work together to address systemic racism and ensure equality for everyone.

Interviewer: How have you been thinking about the issues Black Lives Matter raises?

Agent: I've been trying to educate myself more about the history and the current racial disparities in the U.S. justice system.

Interviewer: How have you been thinking about race in the U.S. recently?

Agent: Recently, I've been thinking about race in the U.S. as an ongoing struggle that requires both awareness and active participation to address disparities.

Interviewer: What about people you're close to? How have they responded to the increased focus on race and/or racism and policing?

Agent: People I'm close to have generally been proactive; many have attended local protests or participated in community discussions.

Interviewer: For you, what makes it easy or hard to stay healthy?

Agent: It is easy for me to stay healthy because I have a supportive community and access to resources like a gym and farmers' market. However, it can be hard when my schedule gets hectic or when I'm traveling.

Interviewer: Tell me about anything big that has happened in the past two years related to your health: any medical diagnoses, flare-ups of chronic conditions, broken bones, pain - anything like that.

Agent: In the past two years, I haven't experienced any significant health issues. I did catch a bad cold last winter, but it resolved on its own after a couple of weeks.

Interviewer: Tell me about anything big that has happened in the past two years related to your health: any medical diagnoses, flare-ups of chronic conditions, broken bones, pain - anything like that.

Agent: In the past two years, I've been fortunate to not have any major health issues. I did have a minor sprain in my ankle that took a few weeks to heal, but nothing more serious.

Interviewer: Sometimes, health problems get in the way. They can even affect people's ability to work or care for their children. How about you?

Agent: Thankfully, my health has not gotten in the way of my work or personal responsibilities. I feel fortunate to be able to maintain a good balance.

Interviewer: Sometimes, health problems get in the way. They can even affect people's ability to work or care for their children. How about you?

Agent: I haven't had any health problems that significantly affected my ability to work or care for my family. I try to address any minor issues promptly to prevent them from becoming major ones.

Interviewer: Sometimes, it's not your health problem, but the health of a loved one. Has this been an issue for you?

Agent: I have had a relative who struggled with a chronic condition, which was challenging for the family. We all tried to support and help as much as we could.

Interviewer: Tell me what it has been like trying to get the health care you or your immediate family need. Have you ever had to forgo getting the health care you need?

Agent: I have been fortunate to have access to good healthcare, but there have been times when waiting to get an appointment took longer than expected. I haven't had to forgo any necessary care.

Interviewer: Have you or your immediate family ever used alternative forms of medicine? This might include indigenous, non-western, or informal forms of care.

Agent: Yes, occasionally we've used herbal remedies passed down through generations for mild conditions and they seem to work well for us.

Interviewer: During tough times, some people tell us they cope by smoking or drinking. How about for you?

Agent: I don't typically cope by smoking or drinking. I prefer to unwind by taking long walks or practicing meditation.

Interviewer: Other people say they cope by relying on prescriptions, pain medications, marijuana, or other substances. How about you and can you describe your most recent experience of using them, if any?

Agent: I don't rely on prescriptions or substances as a primary coping mechanism. I did try medical marijuana for a brief period for anxiety management a while ago.

Interviewer: What are your trusted sources of information about the vaccine?

Agent: I trust reputable sources like the World Health Organization, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and peer-reviewed medical journals for accurate information on vaccines.

Interviewer: Now we're going to talk a bit more about what life was like for you over the past year. Tell me all about how you have been feeling.

Agent: Over the past year, I've had a mixture of emotions. I've experienced stress due to changes in my routine but also found joy in small things and personal growth.

Interviewer: Some people say they struggle with depression, anxiety, or something else like that. How about for you?

Agent: I occasionally experience anxiety, particularly during stressful situations, but I manage it with mindfulness techniques and exercise.

Interviewer: How has it been for your family?

Agent: It's been challenging for my family as well. We've had to adapt to new routines and find ways to support each other emotionally.

Interviewer: Some people say that religion or spirituality is important in their lives, for others not so much. How about you?

Agent: Spirituality plays a moderate role in my life as it provides a sense of peace and grounding during difficult times.

Interviewer: Some people say that religion or spirituality is important in their lives, for others not so much. How about you?

Agent: Spirituality is important to me; it provides comfort and perspective during difficult times.

Interviewer: Some people tell us they use Facebook, Instagram, or other social media to stay connected with the wider world. How about you? Tell me all about how you use these types of platforms.

Agent: I use Instagram to keep up with friends and family, and I occasionally browse Facebook for news updates and community events.

Interviewer: This might be repetitive, but before we go on to the next section, I want to quickly make sure I have this right: who are you living with right now?

Agent: I am currently living with my partner and our two young children.

Interviewer: Anyone who usually lives here but is away - traveling, at school, or in a hospital?

Agent: Yes, one of my roommates is currently away for a semester abroad.

Interviewer: Any lodgers, boarders, or employees who live here?

Agent: No, we do not have any lodgers, boarders, or employees living with us.

Interviewer: Any lodgers, boarders, or employees who live here?

Agent: No, we don't have any lodgers, boarders, or employees living with us.

Interviewer: Who shares the responsibility for the rent, mortgage, or other household expenses?

Agent: My partner and I share the responsibility for rent and other household expenses.

Interviewer: Who shares the responsibility for the rent, mortgage, or other household expenses?

Agent: My partner and I share the responsibility for the rent and household expenses.

Interviewer: Now we'd like to talk about how you make ends meet and what the monthly budget looks like for you and your family. What were your biggest expenses last month?

Agent: Our biggest expenses last month were rent, groceries, and transportation.

Interviewer: How much did your household spend in the past month? Is that the usual amount? And if not, how much do you usually spend and on what?

Agent: Our household spent about $3,000 last month, which is fairly typical. We usually spend the most on rent, groceries, utilities, and transportation.

Interviewer: Does your household own or rent your home?

Agent: We rent our home.

Interviewer: Does your household own or rent your home?

Agent: We own our home.

Interviewer: Bills can fluctuate over the course of a year. Seasons change, there are holidays and special events, school starts and ends, and so on. Tell me all about how your bills have fluctuated over the past year.

Agent: Bills typically increase in winter due to heating costs and around holidays for additional expenses. In summer, utility bills might go up due to air conditioning.

Interviewer: Tell me all about how you coped with any extra expenses in the past months.

Agent: We coped with extra expenses by cutting down on non-essential purchases and using some savings.

Interviewer: Tell me all about how you coped with any extra expenses in the past months.

Agent: To cope with extra expenses, we've been tightening our budget by cutting down on non-essential spending and sometimes dipping into our savings when necessary.

Interviewer: Some people have student loans or credit card debt. Others take out loans from family or friends or find other ways of borrowing money. Tell me about all the debts you're paying on right now.

Agent: Currently, I'm paying off student loans and have a small amount of credit card debt that I'm managing.

Interviewer: Tell me about any time during the past year that you haven't had enough money to buy something that you needed or pay a bill that was due.

Agent: There was one instance last year when I couldn't afford an unexpected car repair right away, but I managed to cover it after adjusting my budget.

Interviewer: What is or was your occupation? In this occupation, what kind of work do you do and what are the most important activities or duties?

Agent: I am a graphic designer. My work primarily involves creating visual concepts and designs for digital and print media.

Interviewer: In the past year, how many weeks did you work (for a few hours, including paid vacation, paid sick leave, and military service)?

Agent: I worked for about 48 weeks in the past year, taking some time off for a vacation and holidays.

Interviewer: How many hours each week did you usually work?

Agent: I usually work around 40 hours each week.

Interviewer: Did you have more than one job or business, including part time, evening, or weekend work?

Agent: No, I did not have more than one job or business.

Interviewer: Did you have more than one job or business, including part time, evening, or weekend work?

Agent: No, I did not have more than one job or business.

Interviewer: For your job or occupations, how much money did you receive in the past month?

Agent: I received $3,500 in the past month.

Interviewer: How often do you get paid?

Agent: I get paid bi-weekly.

Interviewer: Switching gears a bit, let's talk a little about tax time. Did you file taxes last year (the most recent year)?

Agent: Yes, I did file taxes last year.

Interviewer: Switching gears a bit, let's talk a little about tax time. Did you file taxes last year (the most recent year)?

Agent: Yes, I filed taxes last year.

Interviewer: How would you describe your relationships at work? (How is your relationship with your manager or boss? How are your relationships with your coworkers?)

Agent: My relationships at work are very positive. I have a supportive manager and get along well with my coworkers.

Interviewer: How would you describe your relationships at work? (How is your relationship with your manager or boss? How are your relationships with your coworkers?)

Agent: I have a great relationship with my manager and coworkers; we collaborate well and support each other.

Interviewer: Tell me about how predictable your work schedule is. How would you describe your job in terms of flexibility with your hours?

Agent: My work schedule is fairly predictable, but there's some flexibility for adjusting hours when needed.

Interviewer: Some people say it's hard to take or keep a job because of child care. How about for you?

Agent: Fortunately, child care is not a problem for me in maintaining my job.

Interviewer: Do you receive any payments or benefits from SNAP, food stamps, housing voucher payments, supplemental security income, or any other programs like that?

Agent: No, I do not receive any benefits from programs like SNAP or supplemental security income.

Interviewer: Overall, how do you feel about your financial situation?

Agent: Overall, I feel cautiously optimistic about my financial situation. While I'm not wealthy, I have a steady income and a plan for managing expenses and savings.

Interviewer: Are you now married, widowed, divorced, separated, or have you never been married? If you are not currently married, are you currently living with a romantic partner?

Agent: I have never been married, but I am currently living with my romantic partner.

Interviewer: For our records, we also need your date of birth. Could you please provide that?

Agent: My date of birth is April 15, 1990.

Interviewer: Were you born in the United States? If you were not born in the U.S., what country were you born, and what year did you first come to the U.S. to live?

Agent: Yes, I was born in the United States.

Interviewer: Were you born in the United States? If you were not born in the U.S., what country were you born, and what year did you first come to the U.S. to live?

Agent: Yes, I was born in the United States.

Interviewer: Are you of Hispanic, Latinx, or Spanish origin?

Agent: No, I am not of Hispanic, Latinx, or Spanish origin.

Interviewer: What race or races do you identify with?

Agent: I identify as Caucasian.

Interviewer: What is the highest degree or grade you've completed?

Agent: The highest degree I have completed is a Bachelor's degree.

Interviewer: Are you enrolled in school?

Agent: No, I am not enrolled in school.

Interviewer: Are you enrolled in school?

Agent: No, I am not currently enrolled in school.

Interviewer: What religion do you identify with, if any?

Agent: I identify as agnostic.

Interviewer: Generally speaking, do you usually think of yourself as a Democrat, a Republican, an Independent, or what? And how strongly do you associate with that party?

Agent: I usually think of myself as an Independent.

Interviewer: What was the city and state that you lived in when you were 16 years old?

Agent: I lived in Austin, Texas when I was 16 years old.

Interviewer: Did you live with both your own mother and father when you were 16?

Agent: Yes, I lived with both my own mother and father when I was 16.

Interviewer: Who else did you live with?

Agent: I also lived with my younger sister.

Interviewer: Who else did you live with?

Agent: I also lived with my younger brother.

Interviewer: What's the highest degree or grade your dad completed?

Agent: My dad completed a bachelor's degree.

Interviewer: What's the highest degree or grade your mom completed?

Agent: My mom completed her high school education.

Interviewer: What's the highest degree or grade your mom completed?

Agent: My mom completed a bachelor's degree in education.

Interviewer: Did your mom work for pay for at least a year while you were growing up?

Agent: Yes, my mom worked for pay for several years while I was growing up.

Interviewer: Did your mom work for pay for at least a year while you were growing up?

Agent: Yes, my mom worked for pay for several years while I was growing up.

Interviewer: What was her job? What kind of work did she do? What were her most important activities or duties?

Agent: She was a nurse. Her most important duties included caring for patients, administering medication, and providing support to doctors during medical procedures.

Interviewer: What kind of place did she work for? What kind of business was it? What did they make or do where she worked?

Agent: She worked for a local hospital. It was a healthcare facility providing medical services to the community.

Interviewer: Did your dad work for pay for at least a year while you were growing up?

Agent: Yes, my dad worked for pay throughout my childhood.

Interviewer: What kind of place did he work for? What kind of business was it? What did they make or do where he worked?

Agent: He worked for a construction company that specialized in electrical contracting. They focused on building and infrastructure projects.

Interviewer: We all have hopes about what our future will look like. Imagine yourself a few years from now. Maybe you want your life to be the same in some ways as it is now. Maybe you want it to be different in some ways. What do you hope for?

Agent: I hope to have a stable career in my field, a happy family life, and the opportunity to travel and explore new cultures.

Interviewer: What do you value the most in your life?

Agent: I value my family and close relationships the most in my life.

Interviewer: And that was the last question I wanted to ask today. Thank you so much again for your time. It was really wonderful getting to know you through this interview.

Agent: Thank you for the interview. It was a pleasure sharing my experiences with you.

Interviewer: And that was the last question I wanted to ask today. Thank you so much again for your time. It was really wonderful getting to know you through this interview.

Agent: Thank you for the opportunity to share my experiences. It was great speaking with you too.
